record.question: Devil’s advocate
record.explanation: Page 7 directions ask for the meaning of the idiom; the only figurative option is 'one who is against religion', since a devil's advocate pleads the devil's (adversary's) cause against God/religion, whereas 'an advocate of a Devil' and 'an advocate like a Devil' are merely literal readings of the words and 'discussion of an advocate' is unrelated. Confidence is only medium because no option gives the standard idiomatic sense (one who argues against a proposition or champions an unpopular cause for the sake of debate), so the item is partly defective.
record.direction: Directions (Questions 58-66): Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrases.
